clue.text: Is of use when a number set sail

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number

indicators.note: to set something is to arrange it, so the letters of sail are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship's crew is useful when they hoist the sails and get under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges SAIL into AILS, which follows A and V.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of help or benefit, so it avails means it serves a purpose.

clue.text: Supports used by printers

definitions.meaning: shelf ... are wall fittings that hold shelves up
the typographic marks printers set round words

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: angled wall fixings that bear weight, and the paired typographical marks.

clue.text: He's old and confused

definitions.note: the definition reads as a man's identity: he is someone with this name

indicators.note: a confused arrangement suggests jumbled order, so the letters of old and are mixed

explanation.surface: A remark about an elderly man who has grown muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' scrambles OLD AND into the man's name; the definition is just 'He's', a fellow with a given name.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, so it is a fair way to say who 'he' is.

clue.text: Intercept an order to execute?

definitions.meaning: to block or cut off someone before they arrive
a command to behead someone, read literally as remove the head

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to block someone's path; read literally it orders a beheading.

clue.text: Sharp practice produces uproar

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fraudulent scheme and a loud din, two everyday senses.

clue.text: Love romance novel, set in Africa

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A love story written as a book, with its action placed in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges O plus ROMANCE into the country; 'novel' looks like the noun for a book but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is a nation on the west coast of central Africa, so it lies in that continent.

clue.text: Subdue superior force

parts.note: over means above or higher in rank
power is strength or force

explanation.surface: Bringing someone under control with stronger force.
explanation.definitionFit: To overpower an opponent is to subdue them by greater strength.

clue.text: Can an obese man have such an attraction?

definitions.text: Can an obese man have such an attraction?

parts.words: Can an obese man have such an attraction?
parts.note: a portly fellow called Al would be a ..., giving the deadly allure of the film title

explanation.definitionFit: A deadly allure, as in the film title; the clue also splits it into a plump man named Al.

clue.text: Fish and chips cooked with lard

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over and changed, as in cooking the books

explanation.surface: A chip-shop order: fish and chips fried in lard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges CHIPS and LARD together; 'Fish and chips' looks like one dish but 'Fish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small oily sea fish of the herring family, often sold tinned.

clue.text: Heavens above!

parts.note: an exclamation of surprise, read literally as the firmament overhead

explanation.definitionFit: The heavens are the expanse overhead, poetically the firmament; the exclamation is taken literally.

clue.text: It's said to give equal support

indicators.note: said tells us the word for equal is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a peer is one's equal in rank or age

explanation.surface: Something claimed to offer even, balanced support.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar holding up a bridge or arch is a structural support of this kind.

clue.text: Dances arranged to scale

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of dances are reordered

explanation.surface: Dance routines set out according to proportion, as on a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges DANCES; 'to scale' looks like a drawing term but means climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a mountain is to climb it, a synonym of going up.

clue.text: False story about ringleader produces bad feeling

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the story goes round the letter

parts.note: fiction is an invented story
the leader, or first letter, of ring is R

explanation.surface: A lie told about the chief troublemaker stirs up resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction between people is conflict or animosity arising from disagreement.

clue.text: A fault in a fool or comic

indicators.note: in places the fault inside the word for fool

parts.note: a mug is slang for a gullible fool
a sin is a moral fault

explanation.surface: Spotting a flaw in a clown or comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts SIN inside MUG, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic and the answer are both adjectives meaning funny or entertaining.

clue.text: Shows appreciation, rises

definitions.meaning: of a sum or value, to appreciate is to grow in worth

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means accumulates or increases, as values do when they appreciate.

clue.text: A love outwardly secure

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so nil is wrapped around the letter A

parts.note: love is a score of zero, nil

explanation.surface: A sweetheart who appears confident and settled on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure something in place is to fasten it, as by hammering in a metal pin.

clue.text: It may identify member leading the orchestra

indicators.note: leading means coming first, so arm goes before the next piece

parts.note: an arm is a limb, or member, of the body
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: Something marking out the player who heads the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member leading the orchestra' sounds like the conductor or leader; it is ARM placed before BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A band worn round the sleeve marks out a captain, official or mourner.

clue.text: By no means on one's uppers

definitions.meaning: having no means at all, without money
British idiom for very poor, with shoes worn down to the uppers

explanation.definitionFit: Being insolvent means having no means and being destitute, which both phrases describe.

clue.text: Free of duty

parts.note: reads like tax-exempt, but means taking over someone's watch so they may go

explanation.definitionFit: To take over from a guard or worker, releasing them from their shift.

clue.text: Marsh has meeting put into the paper

indicators.note: put into means the meeting is placed inside the paper

parts.note: a quire is a quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets
AGM is an annual general meeting

explanation.surface: A news report that a wetland has been the subject of a meeting in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into' puts AGM inside QUIRE; 'paper' looks like a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog or soft wet ground where one sinks, much like a marsh.

clue.text: Order a hose connection

definitions.meaning: the Order of the ... is England's senior order of knighthood
a band that holds up stockings, or hose

explanation.definitionFit: Both the highest English knightly order and a stocking band carry this name.

clue.text: Vessel takes girl to see the country

parts.note: a can is a container, or vessel
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A ship picks up a young woman to go sightseeing abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a North American nation, so a country.

clue.text: Plant in haste, losing it

indicators.note: losing means the word it is dropped out

parts.note: celerity is swiftness or haste

explanation.surface: Putting something in the ground hurriedly and mislaying it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes IT from CELERITY; 'Plant' looks like a verb but is the definition noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable grown for its crisp stalks, so a type of plant.

clue.text: Governess is expected to bring the girl up

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the girl's name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A nanny is supposed to raise the young lady of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ANN to NNA after DUE; 'bring up' looks like raising a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone or governess, especially in Spain, looking after a young woman.

clue.text: Go hunting, we hear, for a bird

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is spoken and replaced by one that sounds alike

parts.note: to stalk is to pursue prey stealthily

explanation.surface: Setting off on a hunt for a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird, the kind said to deliver babies.

clue.text: They held people in ridicule

parts.note: wooden frames that locked offenders' heads and hands for public scorn; the verb also means to mock

explanation.definitionFit: These were stocks-like frames used for public humiliation, holding offenders up to scorn.

clue.text: They are defrauded of a penny in fees

indicators.note: in means the penny is placed inside the fees

parts.note: dues are fees paid for membership
p is the abbreviation for a British penny in decimal money

explanation.surface: People who were cheated out of a penny in their charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P inside DUES; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Victims of a swindle are those fooled or cheated, the plural noun matching 'They'.

clue.text: To squander money proves wrong — object to it

indicators.note: wrong means not right, so the letters of proves are put out of order

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Someone argues that wasting money is wrong and objects to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges PROVES to OVERSP, then END goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend more than one can afford is to waste money.
